headline: Renting Nvidia H100 AI chips on one-year contracts costs 60% more than a year ago, consulting firm SemiAnalysis says, as AI firms scramble for computing power.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: one price figure from the consulting firm SemiAnalysis, relayed second-hand, with no date for the original Wall Street Journal report.
importance_line: Rising rental prices and tougher contracts squeeze AI start-ups first and then larger AI labs, but the 60% figure is a single consulting firm's estimate for one chip and one contract type.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports, as relayed by BGNES, that SemiAnalysis, a consulting firm that tracks AI data, puts the hourly price of renting Nvidia H100 chips on a one-year contract 60% higher than a year ago, as AI companies, venture-capital firms and executives compete for scarce computing capacity. Cloud providers are increasingly asking for contracts of several years with up to 30% paid in advance, according to the report, and some firms are signing for more capacity than they need or trying to resell what they cannot use.
notes: Original Wall Street Journal article not seen; BGNES relays it, so the WSJ is credited as the reporter and the BGNES link is used. WSJ publication date not stated. The 60% figure is SemiAnalysis's, quoted by the WSJ.
